publication: Pankratz, L. B. (1982), Thermodynamic Properties of Elements and Oxides, U.S. Bureau of Mines Bulletin 672.

P672-T80.source_note: Table 80, printed p. 80; the 49.500 kcal/mol 298 K anchor is the elemental formation-table value. Thermal data are transcribed from the published row.

P672-T81.source_note: Table 81, printed p. 81; the 52.600 kcal/mol 298 K anchor is the elemental formation-table value. High-temperature nodes are transcribed from the published row.

P672-T82.source_note: Table 82, printed p. 82; the -137.160 kcal/mol 298 K anchor is the elemental formation-table value. The printed liquid branch begins at the 1098 K fusion marker.

P672-T102.source_note: Table 102, printed p. 102; the -61.700 kcal/mol 298 K anchor is from the elemental formation table and CODATA. Other thermal data from Mills.

P672-Se-g.source_note: Pankratz Bulletin 672 selenium gas table, printed p. 367; 56.250 kcal/mol is derived from the printed 0.5 Se2(g)=Se(g) reaction value, 39.600 kcal/mol, plus half the printed Se2(g) elemental formation value, 33.300 kcal/mol. It is not a printed formation-table cell. Thermal data from Mills (158).

P672-Se2-g.source_note: Pankratz Bulletin 672 selenium gas table, printed pp. 368-369; the 33.300 kcal/mol 298 K anchor is the elemental formation-table value. Data from Mills (158). Printed entropy nodes at 1400 K and 1800 K match the scan, and the printed Cp equation agrees within rounding.

P672-Te-g.source_note: Table 415, printed p. 415; 50.600 kcal/mol is derived from the printed 0.5 Te2(g)=Te(g) reaction value, 31.435 kcal/mol, plus half the printed Te2(g) elemental formation value, 38.330 kcal/mol. It is not a printed formation-table cell. Data from Mills (158).

P672-Te2-g.source_note: Table 416, printed p. 416; 38.330 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor. Source prints 100 K Cp, entropy, and enthalpy nodes to 2000 K; data from Mills (158).

P672-TeO2-g.source_note: Tellurium Dioxide gas table, printed pp. 420-421; -15.100 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor on p. 420. Thermal data from Spoliti (210); formation enthalpy at 298 K from Muenow (164).

P672-SeO2-g.table: Selenium Dioxide gas table, printed pp. 380-381
P672-SeO2-g.equation_node_note: At the printed 958 K boiling node, the table gives Cp=13.251 cal/(mol K), S=76.781 cal/(mol K), and H-H298=8.123 kcal/mol. The published equations give Cp=13.160152, S=76.754946, and H-H298=8.086592, respectively. The runtime high interval fits the published equations through 1500 K; the printed 958 K row is retained as source data.
P672-SeO2-g.source_note: Elemental formation enthalpy is from the formation table on printed p. 380; gas data from Behrens et al. (12), reaction table on printed p. 381. Printed 1000-1500 K Cp, S, and H-H298 nodes are source data. At the printed 958 K boiling node, Cp/H/S disagree with the published heat-capacity and enthalpy equations by 0.090848 cal/(mol K), 0.036408 kcal/mol, and 0.026054 cal/(mol K); the printed node is retained.

P672-SeO-g.table: Selenium Oxide gas table, printed pp. 376-377
P672-SeO-g.source_note: The elemental formation table on printed p. 376 gives ΔfH°298 = 12.750 kcal/mol; the reaction table on printed p. 377 gives -3.900 kcal/mol for 0.5 Se2(g)+0.5 O2(g)=SeO(g). Cp, S, and H-H298 nodes and thermal data are from Gordon (81).

P672-SeO2-c.source_note: Table 378, printed p. 378; -53.860 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor. The source labels the 413-602 K region estimated and marks 602 K as the SeO2 sublimation point; source equations extend through 602 K.

P672-TeO2-l.table: Tellurium Dioxide condensed-phase formation table, printed p. 418
P672-TeO2-l.source_note: The elemental-formation table on printed p. 418 gives the -77.100 kcal/mol 298 K anchor; the separate reaction table on p. 419 gives -96.265 kcal/mol for 0.5 Te2(g)+O2(g)=TeO2(l). Source marks the 1006 K melting point and 6.760 kcal/mol fusion enthalpy; liquid Cp is 27.600 cal/(mol K). Formation anchor and entropy from Wagman (236); high-temperature liquid data based on Prescher (186) and Mezaki (154).

P672-As-g.source_note: As(g), printed p. 49; 72.120 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor, while the high-temperature table relates gas thermochemistry to the 1/4 As4(g) reference. Thermal data from Hultgren (99).

P672-As2-g.source_note: As2(g), printed p. 50; 52.820 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor. Thermal data from Hultgren (99); source reaction is 2As[cr, 1/4As4(g)] = As2(g).

P672-As4-g.source_note: As4(g), printed p. 52, ideal tetratomic row; 36.640 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor. The ideal triatomic label belongs to As3(g) on p. 51. Thermal data from Hultgren (99).

P672-As4O6-g.source_note: Table 56, printed p. 56; -285.910 kcal/mol is the 298 K elemental formation-table anchor. Above 876 K, the printed enthalpy-of-formation column switches to the 1/4 As4(g) reference; stored 298 K formation remains on the crystal reference. Data from Behrens and Rosenblatt (13).

P672-As2O3-c.source_note: Table 53, printed p. 53; -157.020 kcal/mol is the elemental formation-table anchor. Above 360 K data are estimated; low-temperature heat capacity and S298 from Chang (29), formation enthalpy from Wagman (236).
